question.prompt: It takes Mary \(30\) minutes to walk uphill \(1\) km from her home to school, but it takes her only \(10\) minutes to walk from school to home along the same route. What is her average speed, in km/hr, for the round trip?

solutions.explanation:
Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total travel time. Mary walks the same \(1\)-km route in each direction, so the round-trip distance is \(2\) km.

The total time is \(30+10=40\) minutes, which is \(40/60=2/3\) hour. Therefore her average speed is
\[
\frac{2}{2/3}=3\text{ km/hr}.
\]
The answer is \(\boxed{3\text{ km/hr}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
solutions.title: Use total distance and total time
